start.title: A Hidden Wound
start.text:
Beneath your armor, the leprosy spreads.
A young Israelite servant whispers of a prophet.

choices.feedback: Pride keeps your wound hidden.
Silence will not heal you.
2 Kings 5:3 — The servant girl told her mistress that the prophet in Samaria could cure Naaman of his leprosy.

curse_consequence.title: Soften Your Heart
curse_consequence.text:
Her words are not a threat.
They may be the only door open to you.

choices.feedback: You set down your pride and listen.

hide_consequence.title: No More Hiding
hide_consequence.text:
The mark grows beneath your armor.
Only truth can lead to healing.

choices.feedback: You turn to her quiet voice.

journey.title: Letters and Gold
journey.text:
The king sends silver, gold, and a letter.
The road to Israel waits.

choices.feedback: 2 Kings 5:4-6 — Naaman went to the king of Aram, who then sent a letter and gifts to the king of Israel, not directly to the prophet.
The Lord works through His servant.

king_consequence.title: Not by Royal Hand
king_consequence.text:
Israel's king tears his robe in fear.
The prophet sends word: come to him.

choices.feedback: You turn the chariot toward Elisha.

arrival.title: A Closed Door
arrival.text:
Your chariot waits at the prophet's house.
Elisha does not come out.

choices.feedback: 2 Kings 5:10 — Elisha sent a messenger to Naaman with instructions, rather than coming out himself.
Healing is not seized.
Grace is not bought.

force_consequence.title: Lower Your Sword
force_consequence.text:
Strength will not heal your skin.
Wait, and listen.

choices.feedback: You step back from the door.

gold_consequence.title: Treasures Will Not Cleanse
gold_consequence.text:
Your silver cannot reach the wound.
The prophet asks no payment.

choices.feedback: You gather the coins back in.

instruction.title: Wash Seven Times
instruction.text:
The messenger speaks for the prophet.
"Wash in the Jordan and be clean."

choices.text: Refuse — the rivers at home are better
choices.feedback: 2 Kings 5:11-12 — Naaman was angry and turned away, believing the rivers of Damascus were better than the Jordan.
God does not need a stage.
Humble counsel softens stone.

refuse_consequence.title: If It Were a Great Thing
refuse_consequence.text:
Your servants whisper at your side.
"If he had asked something hard, would you not do it?"

choices.feedback: Their words land deep.

ceremony_consequence.title: Lay Down the Show
ceremony_consequence.text:
There is no parade, no fire, no chant.
Only muddy water and obedience.

choices.feedback: You let go of the spectacle.

jordan.title: Into the Brown Water
jordan.text:
The Jordan flows slow and muddy.
You step in, armor laid aside.

choices.feedback: Half-faith leaves you unchanged.
2 Kings 5:14 — Naaman went down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God.

once_consequence.title: Finish What He Said
once_consequence.text:
His word was seven, not one.
Return into the water.

choices.feedback: You sink beneath the current again.

healed.title: Skin Like a Child
healed.text:
You rise from the water clean.
"Now I know the God of Israel is true."
